messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: Installing RStan and Question about Instructions
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

Jiqiang/Ben,

Can we just change the installation instructions to have people download the tar.gz file and install locally from source? If so, we can just use GitHub to host.

Jiqiang, there was a second reference to google code there. I just edited the wiki removing it.






Daniel






On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 11:42 AM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
That did the trick. I'm using R 3.0.2


On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 11:34 AM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Then put CXX = clang++ in your ~/.R/Makevars 

What version of R are you using?  I wonder the newest version of R for Mavericks (R-3.1.0-mavericks.pkg) has set CXX to clang++ instead of llvm-g++.

Jiqiang 


On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 11:28 AM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Without the Makevars changes I get this error msg:

* installing *source* package ‘rstan’ ...

** package ‘rstan’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked

** libs

** arch - 

llvm-g++-4.2 -arch x86_64 -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include -DNDEBUG -I"../inst/include/stansrc"   -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0"  -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0/unsupported"  -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/boost_1.54.0" -I"../inst/include"  -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -ftemplate-depth-256 -I/usr/local/include -I"/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/Rcpp/include"   -fPIC  -O3  -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o

/bin/sh: llvm-g++-4.2: command not found

make: *** [stanc.o] Error 127

ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘rstan’

* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/rstan’


The downloaded source packages are in

‘/private/var/folders/q7/l6dsv0sx7r9d3gv1zc0_rhp40000gn/T/RtmpnbQpgu/downloaded_packages’

Warning message:

In install.packages("rstan", type = "source") :

  installation of package ‘rstan’ had non-zero exit status

> 


And with the Makevars changes I get this


* installing *source* package ‘rstan’ ...

** package ‘rstan’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked

** libs

** arch - 

clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++ -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include -DNDEBUG -I"../inst/include/stansrc"   -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0"  -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0/unsupported"  -isystem"../inst/include/stanlib/boost_1.54.0" -I"../inst/include"  -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -ftemplate-depth-256 -I/usr/local/include -I"/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/Rcpp/include"   -fPIC  "-mtune=native  -O3 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o

/bin/sh: -c: line 0: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'

/bin/sh: -c: line 1: syntax error: unexpected end of file

make: *** [stanc.o] Error 2

ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘rstan’

* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library/rstan’


The downloaded source packages are in

‘/private/var/folders/q7/l6dsv0sx7r9d3gv1zc0_rhp40000gn/T/RtmpRZlEZV/downloaded_packages’

Warning message:

In install.packages("rstan", type = "source") :

  installation of package ‘rstan’ had non-zero exit status



On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 11:22 AM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Please see comments below.  
Jiqiang 


On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 10:54 AM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm trying to install RStan and Mavericks and I'm getting this error over and over:

Warning: unable to access index for repository http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.2.0.tar.gz/src/contrib

trying URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) : 

  cannot open URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

In addition: Warning message:

In download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :

  cannot open: HTTP status was '403 Forbidden'

Warning in download.packages(pkgs, destdir = tmpd, available = available,  :

  download of package ‘rstan’ failed


I updated the wiki page with a new repo yesterday.  I am not sure why it seems that you saw a previous version of this page.  Try to refresh the webpage?


Also, with regards to the instructions online, it says that ~/.R/Makevars should have the following text:

CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
but that doesn't match
if (!file.exists("~/.R/Makevars")) {
  cat('CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++\n
       CXXFLAGS="-mtune=native  -O3 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion"\n', 
       file="~/.R/Makevars");
} else {
   file.show("~/.R/Makevars");
}


If you are using xcode 5.1, you can leave all of those alone as it is for 5.0.1.  In 5.1, the default template depth is 256 and we don't need -stdlib=libstdc++.  So maybe you don't need to mess with ~/.R/Makevars at all for the most recent xcode.

I think it would make sense to refactor rstan so it is installable via devtools::install_github.  This would require copying the relevant headers into the inst/include directory and commiting them into the repository, since install_github can't do submodules (as far as i know).  But the updating can be automated, memory is cheap, and the ease of installation is significant.  Here's a branch of rstan that is installable via install_github:  https://github.com/jrnold/rstan/tree/install_github.

parts:
On Tuesday, June 24, 2014 4:07:38 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
But actually if llvm-g++ cannot be found, the function would stop during installing Rcpp from source. 

Really? I would assume that R < 3.1 would just ignore CXX_STD and try to install with the default configurations.



I thought it would stop for installing rcpp from source if CXX points to something not found.  I was wrong.  In fact, it would stop for the hello word example.  I intended set my CXX to llvm-g++-4.2, which is not available.  See below:

Right. I would expect it to fail if the user manually sets CXX to some compiler that does not exist on the machine.  That is why install_rstan() ignores ~/.R/Makevars . What I am unclear about is if there is some combination of OS X and Xcode where ignoring ~/.R/Makevars implies both that llvm-g++-4.2 gets used and rstan or Rcpp fails to install. If so, then we would need special instructions for that case.

Ben
